notes: On 6 June 2020, unidentified gunmen attacked Maigoge (Bali LGA, Taraba) and killed 4 residents. The attack is believed to be related to the ongoing Tiv-Jukun conflict in the area.
On 4 September 2021, a soldier opened fire while trying to disperse a crowd during local elections in Gwanki (Makarfi LGA, Kaduna). A girl was killed by a stray bullet.

Around 15 September 2024 (as reported), the Otulu community people protested in Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta) over the alleged seizure of their land by the Ogwashi-Uku people. They displayed placards with various inscriptions calling on the government to intervene and stop the seizure of their land.

On 15 September 2022, officials of Yakurr LGA task force beat up a civilian and caused him some burns on his body in Ugep (Yakurr, Cross River) following the victim's refusal to hand over his car keys to the officials who were dressed in mufti. The assailants fled after the victim was wounded.

On 23 October 2020, Nigerian police forces attacked a journalist in Udu LGA, Delta over the enforcement of the state-wide curfew despite the journalist being on an official assignment. No reported fatalities.

On 14 December 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at their hideout in a forest in Emohua LGA (Rivers) and rescued four abductees. Two members of the group were killed.

Around 30 September 2021 (week of), an unidentified cult group killed four suspected members of a rival group in Kuchibena, near the Life Camp, Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The assailants dismembered the body of one of their victims, chopped off his head and hung it on a stick. The community had been in palpable fear over the incessant cult clashes and killing in the area, prompting the police to request that the slums in the area be demolished. 4 fatalities reported.

On 5 September 2022, a presumed faction of Igbide communal militia killed one person and wounded the vice president of a faction of the community at Igbide (Isoko South, Delta). The two victims were driving together when they were shot by the assailants, soldiers were deployed to the area to restore calm.
Looting: On 26 December 2023, ISWAP raided and looted drugs from a Primary Health Care center in Mainok (Kaga, Borno).

On 13 March 2023, policemen attached to Operation Whirl Punch engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash, after the militia blocked the Galadimawa-Tumbruku road (Giwa, Kaduna). One militia member was killed, others fled with bullet wounds and the policemen recovered one rifle and two live rounds of ammunition.
On 5 August 2024, the Buccaneers and Eiye clashed and killed one person in Ake Junction, Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).

On 15 February 2024, a Naval officer shot and killed a man at a military checkpoint at Owerri-Nta (Isiala Ngwa South, Abia) after he refused to stop at the checkpoint. The Navy claimed that the victim was shot because he was struggling for a gun with the soldier after he was invited over an allegation of theft levelled against him.

On 25 December 2022, a Kaduna militia on motorcycles attacked civilians at Anguwan Aku in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna) and conducted a house to house search. One person was killed; 53 person were abducted, 7 persons among the abductees escaped and 45 others were taken away.

Security measures: On 23 January 2024, the governor of Plateau state imposed a 24 hour curfew on Mangu LGA (Plateau) following violence which broke out in different parts of the town [coded separately].
On 19 May 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted a man and later killed him along the Banki-Kumshe Road near Kumshe (Bama, Borno). They also stole an unspecified number of bicycles belonging to IDPs.

On 6 August 2024, protesters marched, in their large number, to the residence of the former Governor of Rivers State and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). They displayed placards with various inscriptions decrying the high cost of living and alleged bad governance in Nigeria.

On 7 December 2022, members of the Kaduna state chapter of ARPON protested at the Kaduna state police command (Kaduna North, Kaduna) to demand that the National Assembly urgently pass the two police bills that are before the house in order to address the challenges faced by its members.
On 24 July 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed two people in Godiya village, coded as Ruwan Godiya (Faskari, Katsina). An unspecified number of others were injured and abducted.
On 4 October 2021, unidentified armed men shot sporadically while enforcing a sit at home order in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). Casualties unknown. Police sources denied reports of the attack.

On 17 September 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia, killing two in an ambush at Hayin Nakwakina village in Giwa LGA, coded to Hayin Kanwa (Giwa, Kaduna). The troops recovered two motorcycles, a mobile phone, and machetes.
